precepts.text: They watched him, and sent forth spies, which should feign themselves just men. Now I'm going to tell you, there's going to be an explosion, a spiritual explosion, an influx of believers, especially from the Christian church. There's going to be 3,000 one day, 5,000 another day; it's going to happen because the scriptures say that. But we got to be mindful: there will be feigned people. During the time of Christ you had a lot of fake brothers amongst them, so we expect that to be true today.
precepts.point: So this is where you self-examine: am I being a phony, a hypocrite amongst the brethren? Am I walking feignedly? Only you can answer that. You and God know the answer; we don't. If a sister ask us, what about this brother, we can only tell her what you show us. Is he really like that? You got to talk to this guy more in depth, more personally, to find out how they truly are. And some brothers can fake it real good.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
“Think not upon those that have walked feignedly before thee.” To feign means to pretend, to fake, to give a false show of something. And Luke shows feigning in action: “And they watched him, and sent forth spies, which should feign themselves just men, that they might take hold of his words.” They pretended to be just men so they could catch Christ in his words.

During the time of Christ there were a lot of fake brothers among them, so we expect that to be true today. There is going to be an explosion, a spiritual explosion, an influx of believers, especially from the Christian church: 3,000 one day, 5,000 another day. It's going to happen, because the scriptures say it.

But we have to be mindful: there will be feigned people among them. Ezra asks God not to think upon those, “but remember them, which according to thy will have known thy fear.”

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
“And Jesus said unto him, No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God.” That's a hireling: he put his hand to the work and then looked back. Some of y'all are sitting here right now. There is a God; remember that.

This is where you self-examine. Am I being a phony, a hypocrite among the brethren? Am I walking feignedly? Only you can answer that. You and God know the answer; we don't.

Ezra prays that God would think not upon those that walked feignedly, but remember them that have known his fear. The one who looks back from the plough is not fit for the kingdom.

precepts.why:
“Now the just shall live by faith: but if any man draw back, my soul shall have no pleasure in him.” That was the guy who put the talent in the napkin: he drew back.

As we're doing the restructuring, certain captains get asked, why did you move this brother from this position to that position? Oh, he's not the same any more. When he came in, he was on fire; we didn't have to tell him what to do. Now you've got to yell at him, you've got to force him. So drop him down and move him to the side, like we read in 1 Corinthians 6 today.

The Lord has no pleasure in the one who draws back. That is walking feignedly before him, and Ezra asks God to think not upon those, but to remember them that according to his will have known his fear.

precepts.text: Our heart is not turned back, neither have our steps declined from thy way. That's how you got to be. That's how we have to be.
precepts.point: So this is where you self-examine: am I being a phony, a hypocrite amongst the brethren? Am I walking feignedly? Only you can answer that. You and God know the answer; we don't. If a sister ask us, what about this brother, we can only tell her what you show us. Is he really like that? You got to talk to this guy more in depth, more personally, to find out how they truly are. And some brothers can fake it real good.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
Against the hireling who puts his hand to the plough and looks back, and the man who draws back, stands Israel's confession: “Our heart is not turned back, neither have our steps declined from thy way.” That's how you've got to be. That's how we have to be.

The heart that does not turn back and the steps that do not decline are what it means to walk before God unfeignedly. Those are the ones Ezra asks God to remember: “remember them, which according to thy will have known thy fear.”

So examine yourself. Has your heart turned back? Have your steps declined from his way since you first came in on fire? You and God know the answer.

precepts.text: Now the end of the commandment is charity out of a pure heart, and of a good conscience, and of faith unfeigned. Not feigned, not folly.
precepts.point: So this is where you self-examine: am I being a phony, a hypocrite amongst the brethren? Am I walking feignedly? Only you can answer that. You and God know the answer; we don't. If a sister ask us, what about this brother, we can only tell her what you show us. Is he really like that? You got to talk to this guy more in depth, more personally, to find out how they truly are. And some brothers can fake it real good.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
Feign is a verb that means to pretend, to fake, to give a false show of something. It includes pretending an illness: a lot of sisters get Sabbath sick. It includes faking an emotion, or making up an excuse. Remember the brother who used to go around teaching fake it till you make it? Don't raise that man up; he isn't right. To feign means to pretend: you are a fake brother, you are pretending.

Paul sets the opposite: “Now the end of the commandment is charity out of a pure heart, and of a good conscience, and of faith unfeigned.” Unfeigned faith: not feigned, not folly.

The whole end of the commandment is charity from a pure heart and a faith that is not pretended. That is the walk Ezra asks God to remember, and the feigned walk is the one he asks God to think not upon.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
“Seeing ye have purified your souls in obeying the truth through the Spirit unto unfeigned love of the brethren, see that ye love one another with a pure heart fervently.” Unfeigned: don't be fake, don't be phony.

Some brothers can fake it real good. If a sister asks us, what about this brother, we can only tell her what you show us. Is he really like that? She's got to talk to him more in depth, more personally, to find out how he truly is.

That is why the love of the brethren has to be unfeigned, out of a pure heart. Only you and God know whether you are walking feignedly; we only see what you show us.

precepts.text: Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love; in honour preferring one another. Not slothful in business: not lazy concerning God's work. Fervent in spirit: be on fire in your spirit, serving the Lord.
precepts.point: So this is where you self-examine: am I being a phony, a hypocrite amongst the brethren? Am I walking feignedly? Only you can answer that. You and God know the answer; we don't. If a sister ask us, what about this brother, we can only tell her what you show us. Is he really like that? You got to talk to this guy more in depth, more personally, to find out how they truly are. And some brothers can fake it real good.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
“Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love; in honour preferring one another.” That is the unfeigned love of the brethren, real and not put on.

“Not slothful in business”: not lazy concerning God's work. “fervent in spirit”: be on fire in your spirit. “serving the Lord.”

This is the opposite of walking feignedly. The feigned brother came in on fire and now has to be yelled at and forced; the hireling looked back from the plough. The one Ezra asks God to remember, one “which according to thy will have known thy fear”, is kindly affectioned to the brethren, not slothful in God's business, and on fire in spirit, serving the Lord.

precepts.text: Let it not be thy will to destroy them which have lived like beasts. The beasts refer to man.
precepts.point: Now the scriptures substantiate the vision Peter had. The vessel knit at the four corners is Israel, and the beasts within it are men. This is why the nations cannot handle us right now: when we speak, we can use the Bible to explain itself. When they hear it, they think it is everybody. No: God said Israel was the vessel.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
In the vessel were “all manner of fourfooted beasts of the earth, and wild beasts, and creeping things, and fowls of the air.” Peter had to explain to the circumcision, who contended with him, that the fourfooted beasts, the wild beasts, the creeping things and the fowls of the air refer to man. So there had to be scripture to prove it.

Ezra prays: “Let it not be thy will to destroy them which have lived like beasts; but to look upon them that have clearly taught thy law.” There are men who have lived like beasts, and Ezra pleads with God not to destroy them. So we know the beast refers to man.

The vision was not about animals; it was about men. Israel, scattered and living like beasts without the law, is what was let down in that sheet, and Ezra's prayer is that God would spare them and look upon those who teach his law.

precepts.text: A brother said kill means kill the old man, as in Romans 6; but Peter would have needed the Old Testament: thou shalt mortify it as thy creature, and quicken it as thy work. Mortify, deaden, kill the old man, and be quickened.
precepts.point: Rise, Peter: it is time to gather the twelve tribes of Israel. Kill: kill the old man, mortify yourself, discipline yourself. Eat: devour wisdom, learn the scripture. And then go out and teach. But in that time there was no New Testament: Peter would have to explain it to those of the circumcision using the Old Testament.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
“Rise, Peter; kill”. What does kill mean? A brother answered: kill the old man, the old mindset, as it is written in Romans 6. That is right. But in that time there was no New Testament. Peter would have to explain it to those of the circumcision using the Old Testament.

Ezra gives it: “Thou broughtest it up with thy righteousness, and nurturedst it in thy law, and reformedst it with thy judgment. And thou shalt mortify it as thy creature, and quicken it as thy work.” That is what you do. You have to mortify, deaden, kill the old man, and be quickened as God’s work.

That is the “kill” in Peter’s vision. Rise, Peter, and kill the old man. Mortify yourself. Discipline yourself. The man God brings up in his righteousness, nurtures in his law and reforms with his judgment is the man who has put the old man to death.

Only after the old man is killed can you eat, learn the scripture, and then go out and teach. That is the order God gave Peter before sending him to gather the northern kingdom.

precepts.text: Swallow down understanding, O my soul, and devour wisdom: that is the eating; you have to learn. For thou hast agreed to give ear, and art willing to prophesy: after you learn, you go out and prophesy. Rise, Peter: it is time to gather the twelve tribes. Kill the old man; mortify yourself. Eat; devour wisdom. Then go out and prophesy.
precepts.point: Rise, Peter: it is time to gather the twelve tribes of Israel. Kill: kill the old man, mortify yourself, discipline yourself. Eat: devour wisdom, learn the scripture. And then go out and teach. But in that time there was no New Testament: Peter would have to explain it to those of the circumcision using the Old Testament.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
After “kill” comes “eat”. What does eat mean? Learn the scripture. Ezra says it plainly: “Swallow then down, O my soul, understanding, and devour wisdom.” That is the eating. You have to go out and learn.

And after you learn, what do you do? “For thou hast agreed to give ear, and art willing to prophesy: for thou hast no longer space than only to live.” You gave ear, you devoured wisdom, and now you are willing to prophesy. After you learn, you go out and prophesy.

So the whole vision is laid out. Rise, Peter: it is time to gather the twelve tribes of Israel back together. Kill, Peter: kill the old man, mortify yourself. Eat, Peter: devour wisdom. Then go out and prophesy.

This is the Old Testament way Peter would have explained it to those of the circumcision: the eating in the vision was never about unclean beasts, but about swallowing down understanding so he could teach the scattered of Israel.

precepts.text: For unto you is paradise opened, the tree of life is planted, the time to come is prepared, a city is builded, and rest is allowed. Spoken to Israel, not to all nations.
precepts.point: Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief. Rest is entered by labour; that is the paradox the wilderness generation never accepted.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
“For we which have believed do enter into rest.” What is that rest that is promised? Ezra shows it: “For unto you is paradise opened, the tree of life is planted, the time to come is prepared, plenteousness is made ready, a city is builded, and rest is allowed, yea, perfect goodness and wisdom.”

This paradise is spoken to the Israelites. It is not talking about all nations. Paradise opened, the tree of life planted, a city builded and rest allowed: that is what is left to us, the promise “of entering into his rest.”

“For unto us was the gospel preached, as well as unto them.” The gospel did not begin in the book of Matthew; Christ was taught to our forefathers too. But “the word preached did not profit them, not being mixed with faith in them that heard it.” They disobeyed Christ and were moved with unbelief, and their unbelief is what kept them from entering in. “Let us therefore fear”, then, lest any of us come short of the paradise and the rest that is allowed to Israel.

precepts.text: Give us seed unto our heart, and culture to our understanding. Culture is heritage.
precepts.point: Our enemies are the enemies of God, the other nations. Here we are unapologetically biblical; take it up with God.

note.label: There Is No Hate Like Christian Love

precepts.why:
Ezra prayed, “O Lord, if thou suffer not thy servant, that we may pray before thee, and thou give us seed unto our heart, and culture to our understanding, that there may come fruit of it”. Another word for culture is heritage: the same heritage Israel discontinued from in Jeremiah 17, the law of life.

The Psalmist shows it: “If I forget thee, O Jerusalem, let my right hand forget her cunning.” The right hand is your strength, what you work with. And Moses says, “from his right hand went a fiery law for them.” If you forget your identity, your way of life goes with it.

“If I do not remember thee, let my tongue cleave to the roof of my mouth; if I prefer not Jerusalem above my chief joy.” Forget the law and you cannot speak it; your tongue is stuck. Try to talk with your tongue cleaving to the roof of your mouth and you sound crazy. That is how Christians sound to those who know the Bible, with their doctrines; to other Christians they sound fine. We cannot prefer Jerusalem as our chief joy if we do not know we are the Israelites, so we become ordained ministers from the white man's theology schools and seminaries, and we sound like idiots.

So culture to our understanding is what we need back: the identity and the laws that go with it, so that fruit may come of it.

precepts.text: Not a novice, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil. Too much rain on a new seed corrupts it.
precepts.point: Man is formed with God's hands, called his own image, and likened unto the husbandman's seed.

note.label: A Tree Bearing No Fruits

precepts.why:
Ezra says the husbandman's seed perishes “if it come not up, and receive not thy rain in due season; or if there come too much rain, and corrupt it”. The husbandman is the Most High, the seed is the word he sows in us, and the rain is wisdom. Anyone who has planted knows that if too much rain falls on a seed, it does not grow. How can too much rain corrupt a man? Paul shows it: “Not a novice, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil.”

A novice is somebody new in this truth, a beginner. Some brothers come in and catch on real quick. Why would a novice get lifted up with pride? Because he got too much rain, too much wisdom, and he cannot handle it. He starts getting high-minded, and then he falls into the condemnation of the devil: Satan destroys the seed that is in him. That is what it means when the scripture says too much rain can corrupt the seed. Knowledge puffeth up, but charity edifieth.

That is why the heavy teaching is eased off at times. You may love it when the class goes deep, but too much of that wisdom too fast can corrupt you. The deacons have been learning in this truth for over twenty years. When you see them go into certain things, it comes from years of being watered; nobody woke up one day able to break down the scriptures.

So the Most High gives the rain in its season, moderately, as Joel says, “the former rain moderately”, raising the waters little by little, from the ankles to the knees, so that we can handle it. The seed that receives its rain in due season takes root and bears fruit; the novice who is lifted up with pride perishes like the corrupted seed.

precepts.text: Before the throne of the Most High the hosts of angels stand with trembling; the host Jacob saw was the angels.
precepts.point: When the scriptures speak of the Lord of hosts, the hosts are the armies of angels that stand before Him.

note.label: Genesis 32: Wrestling Until the Blessing

precepts.why:
“Whose throne is inestimable; whose glory may not be comprehended; before whom the hosts of angels stand with trembling”. The hosts that stand before the throne of the Most High are the angels. When the scriptures speak of the Lord of hosts, the hosts are the armies of angels that stand before Him.

So the host Jacob saw was the angels. As he departed from Laban, “the angels of God met him”, and he said, “This is God’s host”, and called the place Mahanaim, which means two hosts or camps.

precepts.text: Esdras prayed the same prayer as Moses for Israel, and the Most High answered that the sinners are reserved to the end while he rejoices over the disposition of the righteous.
precepts.point: Esdras prayed the same prayer as Moses for the children of Israel, so precept these two prayers together: pay no attention to the fakers, for they remove themselves, but be merciful to us who have no works of righteousness, for by that mercy thou shalt be called merciful. When we are in the midst of sin we live worse than beasts, for a beast runs on instinct, but we consciously choose to go against the laws of the Most High.

note.label: Deuteronomy 9: Not for Thy Righteousness

precepts.why:
Esdras prayed the same prayer as Moses for the children of Israel, so precept these two prayers together. Moses: “destroy not thy people and thine inheritance, which thou hast redeemed through thy greatness”; “look not unto the stubbornness of this people, nor to their wickedness, nor to their sin”. Esdras: “O look not upon the sins of thy people; but on them which serve thee in truth.”

Pay no attention to the fakers, for they remove themselves: “Think not upon those that have walked feignedly before thee: but remember them, which according to thy will have known thy fear.” And be merciful to us who have no works of righteousness, for by that mercy thou shalt be called merciful: “For if thou hast a desire to have mercy upon us, thou shalt be called merciful, to us namely, that have no works of righteousness.”

“Let it not be thy will to destroy them which have lived like beasts”. When we are in the midst of sin we live worse than beasts, for a beast runs on instinct, but we consciously choose to go against the laws of the Most High.

The Most High answered: “Some things hast thou spoken aright, and according unto thy words it shall be. For indeed I will not think on the disposition of them which have sinned before death, before judgment, before destruction: But I will rejoice over the disposition of the righteous, and I will remember also their pilgrimage, and the salvation, and the reward, that they shall have.” The sinners are reserved to the end, while he rejoices over the disposition of the righteous.

precepts.text: These things have I not shewed unto all men, but unto thee, and a few like thee; the wisdom and understanding of the Lord is for the remnant, not the heathen.
precepts.point: Wisdom and understanding are hid from all living and given only to the few, the remnant of Israel who have the conscience and the ability to choose whom they will serve, not the other nations; we fear the Lord like King David, the greatest warrior to ever fight on the earth, who still trembled at God's judgments.

note.label: Job 28: Where Shall Wisdom Be Found

precepts.why:
“Whence then cometh wisdom? and where is the place of understanding? Seeing it is hid from the eyes of all living”. It is hid, and given only to the few: “These things have I not shewed unto all men, but unto thee, and a few like thee.”

The wisdom and understanding of the Lord is for the remnant, not the heathen. It is hid from all living and given to the remnant of Israel, who have the conscience and the ability to choose whom they will serve, not the other nations. God understands the way thereof and knows the place thereof, and he shows it to a few.

precepts.text: You are fed milk until you can talk, then you start learning the commandments.
precepts.point: But thou art he that took me out of the womb; thou didst make me hope when I was upon my mother's breasts. Christ was on his mother's breast drinking milk growing up until he was of age, and she taught him the commandments; even filled with the Holy Ghost, Deuteronomy 6:7 still applied in their household, which is why at twelve he was in the temple.

note.label: Psalm 22: The Prophecy of Christ on the Cross

precepts.why:
“thou didst make me hope when I was upon my mother’s breasts.” Ezra walks through how the Most High raises a child: “For when the body is fashioned now in the mother’s womb, and thou givest it members, thy creature is preserved in fire and water, and nine months doth thy workmanship endure thy creature which is created in her.” Then “when the time cometh, the womb preserved delivereth up the things that grew in it.”

“For thou hast commanded out of the parts of the body, that is to say, out of the breasts, milk to be given, which is the fruit of the breasts, That the thing which is fashioned may be nourished for a time, till thou disposest it to thy mercy.” You are fed milk until you can talk. Then: “Thou broughtest it up with thy righteousness, and nurturedst it in thy law, and reformedst it with thy judgment.” Then you start learning the commandments.

That is how it was with Christ. He was on his mother's breast drinking milk, growing up until he was of age, and she taught him the commandments. Even filled with the Holy Ghost, Deuteronomy 6:7 still applied in their household, which is why at twelve he was in the temple.

note.label: Wickedness: The Grain of Evil Seed

precepts.why: “The most High hath made this world for many, but the world to come for few.” God made this world for many, but the New Jerusalem for few. He compares it like dust: “There be many created, but few shall be saved.” There’s many created in this world, but few shall be saved. Christians can’t understand.

note.label: | SABBATH MORNING CLASS: When The Harvest Is Ripe

precepts.why: The creature was made subject to vanity when we went into idolatry. “Be not wroth with us but spare thy people, and have mercy upon thine own inheritance: for thou art merciful unto thy creature.” Thou art merciful unto thy creature: the creature subjected to vanity is subjected in hope of that mercy.

note.label: America and the World Will Pay Reparations

precepts.why:
“For when they had taken liberty, they despised the most High”: we got liberty, we ain’t in shackles and chains no more; we got free. We’re only free from physical chains. “Thought scorn of his law, and forsook his ways”: that’s our people right there.

“Moreover they have trodden down his righteous”: his righteous people. “And said in their heart, that there is no God”: they doubt his existence. “Yea, and that knowing they must die”: that is not a question; they must die, that’s what the Bible says. Despising the law of God set before them is why many perish in this life.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why: “For unto you is paradise opened, the tree of life is planted, the time to come is prepared, plenteousness is made ready, a city is builded, and rest is allowed, yea, perfect goodness and wisdom. The root of evil is sealed up from you, weakness and the moth is hid from you”: the moth is this human body. “And corruption is fled into hell to be forgotten”: what’s corruption? This body; it is gone. “Sorrows are passed, and in the end is shewed the treasure of immortality”: the new bodies.

note.label: Affliction: Trump 2.0

precepts.why:
Why do we have to go through affliction, if God loves us? “Behold, I have refined thee, but not with silver; I have chosen thee in the furnace of affliction.” The only way you are going to be chosen is to go through that affliction.

Some brothers and sisters think this is a Christian church, where you come and expect everything to be all lovey-dovey and your life to be perfect. It is not. The only way you gain the Kingdom of Heaven is by enduring affliction; you have to prove to God that you are worthy. You can run around scared like everybody else and say I am not teaching the Bible anymore, or you can do what God says no matter what affliction comes upon you. And he does it for his own sake.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 19 Supper, War & Marriage

precepts.why: “There be many created, but few shall be saved”: one third is a few; that’s not a lot. That’s why the Lord ain’t choosing everybody. You got to know your kids; I look at my kids, and from youth I know which have the spirit of faith and which don’t.

note.label: War With The Beast: Death & Persecution

precepts.why:
Everybody today thinks they understand the Bible, that they have the truth, and that God is dealing with them. God is not dealing with everyone; you will know them by their fruits. But this is when it will be made plain: “Then shall they be known, who are my chosen; and they shall be tried as the gold in the fire.”

The verses before speak of when affliction comes upon us, the great insurrection, when they rise up and persecution starts. That is when you will know who really believes this Bible. Let the government come down on the Israelites, not if but when, when the heathen rage and say let us break their bands asunder, as they are doing in France, and see how many still teach the gospel and stand ten toes down. How many will keep God’s testimonies in affliction? That is when you will know who God’s chosen are.

Build yourselves up and pray that when that day comes you are able to endure. If you are studying, praying and applying, you will endure. If you are fake and phony and full of hatred and sin, you will not.

note.label: BORN IN FIRE & WATER

precepts.why:
First the fire. “Behold, I will make my words in thy mouth fire.” The words of God, this Bible, are the words of fire. The word of God is fire because it burns the hearts and minds and spirits of the wicked when they hear it.

But fire is not only something used to harm. It is also used to heal, to cleanse and to fix; fire is a cleansing agent. So the words of God can be the fire that refines us and makes us better, or we rebel against them and get destroyed by the fire that is yet to come. Fire goes both ways.

note.label: BORN IN FIRE & WATER

precepts.why:
“Is not my word like as a fire? saith the Lord; and like a hammer that breaketh the rock in pieces?” The word of God is strong when it is against the wicked.

Often when we sit in class and hear the word of God, if you have a conscience, if God is dealing with you, you feel conflicted: a certain level of guilt or shame. It burns, it hits your soul a certain way. Some people cry; some people go home and reflect and examine themselves, because the word of God is hard, and depending on how it is brought out it can hit hard. But if the person is wicked and rebellious, it burns and they get mad, bitter and angry, and they leave, or they walk around with bitterness in their heart and don’t last long. They get broken in pieces: their spirit gets angry, they get offended, and they’re gone. The word of God is fire both ways.

note.label: BORN IN FIRE & WATER

precepts.why:
“He that feareth the Lord will do good, and he that hath the knowledge of the law shall obtain her.” The context is the knowledge of the law.

“He himself made man from the beginning, and left him in the hand of his counsel”: he made Adam and left Adam in his counsel; he gave Adam his laws. “If thou wilt, to keep the commandments, and to perform acceptable faithfulness.” Faith is a performance, not a thought or a feeling. Faith is a performance, an act: works, doings. The apologists have the audacity to use the Septuagint against us; Sirach is in the Septuagint, and if they read this it would destroy them.

“He hath set fire and water before thee.” But you already had that set before you in the womb: you are preserved in fire and water. Then you come out of the womb and fire and water are set before you again. Why? So you can develop like the child in the womb, so you can grow and be born again.

“Stretch forth thy hand unto whether thou wilt”: you make the choice. “Before man is life and death; and whether him liketh shall be given him.” Whichever you choose, you are going to get. But you are going to go through both, fire and water, and you are going to receive your reward.

note.label: BORN IN FIRE & WATER

precepts.why:
“And by a prophet the Lord brought Israel out of Egypt.” By a prophet, Moses, the Lord brought Israel out of Egypt: going back to Ezekiel 16:1-9.

“And by a prophet was he preserved.” Remember through Ezekiel the Lord said our navel was not cut, we were not washed, and we were not salted. What does salt do? Salt preserves; it is a preservative. The commandments of God are referred to as salt.

Who was preserved? The nation of Israel was preserved by Moses. When Moses gave us the commandments of God, he gave us that salt in ourselves. We became fashioned again anew, serving the peculiar commandments, as Wisdom of Solomon 19:6 says.

note.label: BORN IN FIRE & WATER

precepts.why:
“Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour”: if we stop keeping the commandments of God, “wherewith shall it be salted?” What is it worth? “It is thenceforth good for nothing.”

Because what is salt good for? Preserving. Preservation, preserves, preservatives: it is all the same. That is what the commandments do for us: they keep us from hurt.

note.label: BORN IN FIRE & WATER

precepts.why: “Salt is good: but if the salt have lost his saltness, wherewith will ye season it? Have salt in yourselves.” What is the salt? The commandments of God, that preserve you and keep you alive. If you have salt in you, you are preserved. “And have peace one with another”: be at peace with one another.

note.label: BORN IN FIRE & WATER

precepts.why:
“Neither do men put new wine into old bottles.” The new wine goes into the commandments of God: that is the new man. When you are fashioned again anew, when you become a new creature, you have to put old things away, because the new can’t be kept in the old; otherwise it is no good. New wine in old bottles will not hold; the bottle is worn out, and it rips.

“Else the bottles break, and the wine runneth out, and the bottles perish.” If the body is not changed, it is not going to hold the commandments; it will not keep the commandments of God. If you are still in the world doing worldly things while keeping the commandments of God, you can’t serve both. Eventually it leaks out: after a while you are going to be offended, and you’re going to fall out. If you are going to be new, you have to be new all the way through.

“But they put new wine into new bottles, and both are preserved.” That is being born again: new wine in a new bottle. You keep the commandments of God, you are able to preserve the commandments, and you preserve yourself.

note.label: BORN IN FIRE & WATER

precepts.why:
“Remember Lot’s wife.” Why does it start with that? Lot’s wife looked back because she loved the world she was in, rather than escaping that flame. She looked back, she got destroyed, and she was turned to salt.

“Whosoever shall seek to save his life shall lose it.” If you seek to save or preserve your life in this world, you are going to be destroyed: seeking to save your worldly lifestyle, your job, your worldly family, kids, mothers, fathers, holding on to worldly things. That is the new wine in the old bottle: it ain’t going to hold for long. Eventually it runs out of you, because you haven’t fully changed; the wine is new, but the body and the mind are the same.

“And whosoever shall lose his life shall preserve it.” Whoever loses his life, whoever dies, is killed for this truth, shall preserve his life: not this life here, the life to come. You are going to come back again, better, and live forever. It is the same as the little chastisement in Wisdom of Solomon 3: the torment, and then peace.

note.label: BORN IN FIRE & WATER

precepts.why:
“Let the sighing of the prisoner come before thee.” The prisoner is us. The sighing of the prisoner is our prayers in the time of affliction, persecution, temptation, trouble, perils and dangers.

“According to the greatness of thy power preserve thou those that are appointed to die.” That is why Christ said, those that seek to save their life lose it, and those that lose their life preserve it. They are at peace. The mother with the seven sons: they’re good; they are sealed.

“And render unto our neighbours sevenfold into their bosom their reproach, wherewith they have reproached thee, O Lord. So we thy people and sheep of thy pasture will give thee thanks for ever.” The Most High is making it clear our neighbours, the nations, are going to face a fierce reproach and judgment, sevenfold into their bosom, for what they did against us. But we get preserved. We are going to be all right.

note.label: BORN IN FIRE & WATER

precepts.why:
This whole psalm is about preservation: preserve, preserve, preserve. “The Lord shall preserve thee from all evil: he shall preserve thy soul.”

“The Lord shall preserve thy going out”: leaving this world, “and thy coming in”: coming into this world, “from this time forth, and even for evermore.” Those who are predestined to be preserved are going to be preserved regardless. Whether they die or live, going out or coming in, they are preserved. They’re good.

note.label: BORN IN FIRE & WATER

precepts.why:
“It is a light thing that thou shouldest be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel.” The preserved of Israel are the elect of us.

“I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles”: the Gentiles here are the northern kingdom, not the other nations; they get the light during their slavery. “That thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth”: because Israel is scattered throughout all the ends of the earth, and that is where salvation is going to be brought to them.

note.label: BORN IN FIRE & WATER

precepts.why:
“And Eleazar the priest said unto the men of war which went to the battle.” Notice Eleazar is speaking to the men of war. “Only the gold, and the silver, the brass, the iron, the tin, and the lead”: these are the metals.

“Every thing that may abide the fire, ye shall make it go through the fire, and it shall be clean.” Fire is a cleansing agent as well as a destructive one. “Nevertheless it shall be purified with the water of separation.” Then it goes to the water. So it is cleaned through fire and purified through water, because water is a destructive agent as well as a cleansing agent. The water of separation is the water of sanctification: separation sanctifies; it is made holy.

“And all that abideth not the fire ye shall make go through the water.” What can’t go through the fire goes through the water. But it is supposed to go through both.

note.label: BORN IN FIRE & WATER

precepts.why:
Eleazar spoke to the men of war about the gold and the silver. Who is Paul talking to? “Thou therefore endure hardness, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ.” Endure hardness: that goes into the fire, the affliction, the sorrow, the travail, the narrow, the strait things. A good soldier is a man of war.

“No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life; that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier.” Now you know who he is talking to: the same men of war that Eleazar spoke to, the ones who must pass through the fire and the water.

points: Think not upon those that have walked feignedly before thee.
Remember a brother used to go around teaching, fake it till you make it. I said, "Don't raise that negro up. He ain't right."
So to feign means to pretend. You are a fake brother. You are pretending. You give a false show of something.
You can feign that. You got a lot of sisters that get Sabbath sick.
Making up an excuse.

So this is where you self-examine: am I being a phony, a hypocrite amongst the brethren? Am I walking feignedly? Only you can answer that. You and God know the answer; we don't. If a sister ask us, what about this brother, we can only tell her what you show us. Is he really like that? You got to talk to this guy more in depth, more personally, to find out how they truly are. And some brothers can fake it real good.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

points: Ezra say, listen, Lord, I'm going to speak before you not about all races of people, cuz I'm not concerned with them. When it comes to all races, touching man in general, you know best. You got a will for Moab, you got a will for Ammon, you got a will for Ishmael. But touching thy people, for whose sake I am sorry: I'm only concerned with my people, and I'm sorry for the condition of my people. And for thine inheritance, for whose cause I mourn: I only mourn for your inheritance.

note.label: Perilous Times: Judges and Soldiers

points: For Israel, for whom I am heavy: we all heavy for the condition of my people. We see racial tension; you could cut the tension with a knife. The workplaces with Jake and Esau, they ain't the same. Things ain't happy go lucky as they once was. People walking on eggshells afraid to bring up certain things. Other nations are discussing the things going on in the US because racial tensions are high.

And for Jacob, for whose sake I am troubled: so if you watching the news, if you keeping up with current events, if you've been watching and praying, you're going to be troubled; you're going to be heavy as it's written right here. If you watching what's going on and the condition of our people and how we being abused and used in society: they said, yeah, don't give them the death penalty; no, lock them up; we need sweat equity. They said that in 2026: we need sweat equity. Wow.

note.label: Perilous Times: Judges and Soldiers

points: The only time the word culture appears in the Bible: give a seed unto our heart and culture to our understanding, which is where agriculture comes from. When you apply what is taught you are the soil taking in the nutrients, and then you bring forth fruit.

We are all plants: we come from the ground, we need water and sun, chlorophyll is the plant's melanin, and Eve was a cutting taken from Adam. The plant that refuses the fertilizer gets uprooted and thrown into the fire to keep the righteous warm.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

points: As the husbandman soweth much seed upon the ground and planteth many trees, yet the thing that is sown good in his season cometh not up, neither doth all that is planted take root. The husbandman is the Most High and the seed is us. Every seed has its season, and some seeds only grow in harsh conditions, in affliction. Anyone who has planted knows some seeds take root and some do not.

Even so is it of them that are sown in the world: they shall not all be saved. Some who hear the word and sit here will not take root, will stay in their sin and never bear fruit. He that endureth to the end shall be saved.

note.label: A Tree Bearing No Fruits

points: Like as the husbandman's seed perisheth if it come not up and receive not thy rain in due season, or if there come too much rain and corrupt it, even so perisheth man also. Too much rain is too much wisdom too fast; the deacon eases off the heavy teaching because too much can corrupt.

note.label: A Tree Bearing No Fruits

points: Man is formed with God's hands, called his own image, and likened unto the husbandman's seed.

note.label: A Tree Bearing No Fruits

points: Paradise is a city: the tree of life planted, the time to come prepared, plenteousness made ready, a city builded and rest allowed.
That is where Adam was, resting from all his labours of making everything, Christ in Adam resting in his throne on the earth.
Adam was made of the earth, which was not perfect and was fallible, so the stay was temporary, because flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom.

note.label: Escape Thankskilling : Oh God & My Lord

points: And seek out the glory for such as be like thee: such as be like thee is the elect, those elect Israelites that was like Esdras.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Heaven Suffereth Violence

points: For unto you is paradise opened: wait a minute. Unto you, you Israelites, you elect of God, unto you paradise is open.
The tree of life is planted: the tree of life already planted.
A city is builded: what? A city is building.
And rest is allowed: and rest is allowed. The Lord said, "Go ahead and rest."

Yea, perfect goodness and wisdom: so the kingdom of heaven suffering violence is talking about the children of Israel. The children of Israel went into captivity under Rome, all the way into what we know today as America, and we are still suffering violence. But the Bible still calls us the kingdom of heaven, the kingdom of God.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Heaven Suffereth Violence

note.label: 2 Esdras 8: Many Created, but Few Shall Be Saved

note.label: 2 Esdras 8: Many Created, but Few Shall Be Saved

points: It was not his will that men should come to nought: but they which be created have defiled the name of him that made them, and were unthankful unto him which prepared life for them.

note.label: 2 Esdras 8: Many Created, but Few Shall Be Saved

points: These things have I not shewed unto all men, but unto thee, and a few like thee.

note.label: 2 Esdras 8: Many Created, but Few Shall Be Saved

points: “For many great miseries shall be done to them that in the latter time shall dwell in the world”: there’s going to be a lot of miseries in these last days. “Because they have walked in great pride.” People on this earth today walk in great pride, and certain amongst our own people walk in great, great pride, and the pride is going against God’s laws. When our people go to what they call church, that’s great pride. Transgenderism and all that filth: abominations, all of them. All of them have left the living God and all of them shall be judged. All of this is filth, and the Most High is going to bring judgment on their behind. Judgment is coming.

note.label: Pride & Divine Judgment

points: “But understand thou for thyself”: y’all better learn this Bible for yourselves. Although we’re teaching it to you, you better each learn to absorb it, take it in and understand it for yourselves. “And seek out the glory for such as be like thee”: we’re looking for the elect, looking for men and women that truly believe. That’s what we’re doing; that’s the elect we’re looking for.

note.label: Pride & Divine Judgment

points: There is a reason why the Most High brought Trump into power. “Regard not the wicked inventions of the heathen”: don’t regard the laws they create to bring affliction upon us.

“But the desire of those that keep thy testimonies in afflictions.” God wants us to keep his testimonies in affliction. Bad things are going to happen to us, and that is where God wants us to keep his testimonies. If Trump puts out an executive order saying we can’t teach the Bible the way we teach it anymore, affliction is going to come down on us, and what God is looking for is those who do what he said to do while they are being afflicted. This is war.

Some of you might say, I ain’t teaching the Bible no more, I don’t want them to take away my green card or my citizenship. If that is how you are thinking, this ain’t the place for you. Trump 2.0 is about to turn up affliction on the Israelites, but we have to keep the testimony in affliction. If he puts you in Guantanamo Bay, teach the word in Guantanamo Bay. If they deport you back to your country, teach the word over there.

note.label: Affliction: Trump 2.0

points: “Regard not the wicked inventions of the heathen”. We cannot worry about what the heathen invent to do to us: prison, deportation, killing. God says do not fear their inventions. Why? Because of “the desire of those that keep thy testimonies in afflictions.”

This is about keeping God’s testimonies, his laws, in affliction, because that is when the Lord chooses his people, as Isaiah 48 says. When you keep his laws and his testimonies in affliction, that is when he chooses you.

note.label: War With The Beast: Death & Persecution

points: “For thou art alone, and we all one workmanship of thine hands.” We are one workmanship of his hands.

note.label: BORN IN FIRE & WATER

points: “For when the body is fashioned now in the mother’s womb”: keep hearing that word, fashioned, over and over again. “In the mother’s womb”, as we read earlier in Psalms and in Ecclesiastes 11:5. “And thou givest it members”: the members which are written in his book.

“Thy creature is preserved in fire and water.” Keep that word preserved in mind. How is a baby preserved in fire and water? Physically speaking, the fire is the heat in her womb, and the water is what the child is surrounded by, the fluid, the sack. That is science. But there are layers to this.

“And nine months doth thy workmanship endure thy creature which is created in her.” There is a reason behind why the Lord allows a child to form within that time frame. What does a child undergo as they grow in the womb? Change.
We go through fire and water in the womb, and we go through fire and water outside of it too, and we grow thereby the same way outside the womb as we do in the womb. That is how a man is born again.

note.label: BORN IN FIRE & WATER

points: Back to Ezra, so as not to lose the thought. “For when the body is fashioned now in the mother’s womb”: and refashioned again, when you repent. “And thou givest it members”: it grows. “Thy creature is preserved in fire and water.”

“And nine months doth thy workmanship endure thy creature which is created in her.” Nine months the mother endures the child growing within her. The child is growing within the mother, undergoing growth, and with growth comes change. Now, preserved: still going back to being born again.

note.label: BORN IN FIRE & WATER

points: “Thy creature is preserved in fire and water”: preserved in fire, and preserved in water. Now the fire and the water come back together.
